research_question: When KEEP_WARM and FAULT_IN are measured under the same payload, worker counts, batch workload, PSS surface, barriers, and runner, what joint typed frontier remains?

hosted_proxy.run_order: all six combinations then exact reverse

primary_oracles: capability SHA256 identities remain stable in every arm
the complete deterministic job digest map is identical across all six worker/residency arms
FAULT_IN prestart PSS is lower than KEEP_WARM prestart PSS for worker counts 1, 2, and 4
KEEP_WARM has zero logical fault span
FAULT_IN has positive logical fault span and positive resume cost
KEEP_WARM pays positive idle capability byte-seconds
the measured typed frontier is non-empty
no scalar gain is emitted without an external price or hard constraint
critical_boundaries: logical fault span is the per-worker mapped/touched capability span and is not physical SSD/NVMe traffic
PSS is a hosted Linux process-sharing proxy, not universal hardware accounting
this experiment does not impose a synthetic memory cap or claim a universal joint optimum
resource-optimal joint plan does not grant execution authority
next_falsifier: Introduce an explicit finite PSS admission cap and change the observed resource certificate between idle and work phases, then test online joint replanning.
